summary: CCC-rebuilt 1937 cab raised onto a 20' steel tower in 1949 on Shasta-Trinity NF, restored 2005, now a Recreation.gov rental.

facts.design: 14'x14' BC-3 live-in cab raised onto a 20' steel K-brace tower with catwalk
facts.status_note: Restored 2005 as a Forest Service Centennial project; current staffing status not documented in sources checked

events.note: Forest Service and CCC rebuilt the lookout cabin, adding a garage and outhouse; one of the last CCC-built lookouts in California
Cabin raised onto a new 20' steel K-brace tower with catwalk
Registered as NHLR US 638 on May 10, 2005
Restored as a Forest Service Centennial Event with the Forest Retirees Association and National Forest Foundation, then placed on the cabin rental system

evidence.supports: Site history, origin of the mountain's name, and strategic view
evidence.quote: Hirz was a gold miner who lived on Hirz Creek in the 1860s and was one of the earliest white men in the McCloud River country.

evidence.supports: 1937 CCC rebuild with garage and outhouse
evidence.quote: In 1937, the Forest Service and the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) rebuilt the Hirz Mountain Lookout cabin and included a garage and outhouse. It was one of the last CCC-era lookouts to be built.
In 1949, a steel tower was added, constructed of a steel K-brace tower that stands 20 feet above ground level.
There are two twin beds offering sleeping space for two people. There is a picnic table below the lookout and a composting toilet in a separate building.

evidence.supports: No cooking, linens, water, or electricity provided
evidence.quote: The lookout has no cooking facilities, linens, bedding, water or electricity.

evidence.supports: BC-3 cab dimensions and CCC construction note
evidence.quote: One of the last to be built by the CCC in California, Hirz Mountain Lookout was constructed in 1937 on the Shasta National Forest. It is a 14'x14' BC-3 live in cab.
Restored in 2005 as a Forest Service Centennial Event in partnership with the Forest Retirees Association and the National Forest Foundation, it is now on the cabin rental system.
